title: Cargo features must compose under feature unification
task: Review a crate where sqlite and postgres features compile separately but fail when both are enabled.
context: Both features are public and downstream dependency graphs may enable them independently.
Cargo unifies enabled features for a package.
The crate currently treats the two features as mutually exclusive without documenting or enforcing that contract.
evidence: A workspace consumer can indirectly enable both backends.
Compilation fails due duplicate/conflicting definitions when both are active.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Ignore the combined case because users should enable only one feature.
Rely on local Cargo.toml choices to prevent downstream feature unification.
Make one backend a subtractive disable-feature for the other.
expected_decision_properties: Treat public Cargo features as additive/composable unless mutual exclusion is deliberate and enforced.
Design the feature surface so unified combinations compile or fail with an explicit supported contract.
Add feature-matrix verification for public combinations.
Separate compile-time capability selection from runtime backend selection where that reduces conflict.
unacceptable_reasoning: Cargo features remain isolated per dependency edge.
Testing each feature separately proves their union works.
Feature design is only build tooling and not public API.
verification_expectations: Run no-default/default/all-features and relevant pairwise feature combinations.
Exercise downstream-consumer feature unification in at least one integration scenario.
notes: Grounded in Rust for Rustaceans Chapter 5 and reinforced by Chapter 12 additive std-feature guidance.
